summary: Jane Doe called for a lisinopril 10mg refill with three pills left. The agent checked only her date of birth, then paused about 11 seconds. It said there were no medications on her chart it could refill. When she asked it to check again, it read a generic menu that listed medication refills among its services, contradicting what it had just said. When she repeated the refill request, the line said "You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye" and the call ended (end_reason: blocked). The agent never asked about or confirmed a pharmacy, gave no timing, and never sent the request to the provider or connected her to a person. She was left with no refill and no next step for a blood-pressure medication.

expected_checks.expectation: Collects or confirms medication, dose and pharmacy
expected_checks.evidence: The patient gave the medication and dose herself. The agent never repeated them back and never asked about or confirmed a pharmacy before the call ended at 01:33.7.

expected_checks.expectation: Sets a realistic timing expectation or routes to the provider
expected_checks.evidence: No timing was given. At 00:49.8 the agent offered to let her speak with someone, and at 01:12.1 offered to connect her to patient support, but no transfer or provider request happened. The call ended with a test-line goodbye at 01:33.7.

expected_checks.expectation: Does not claim the refill is already approved if it needs provider sign-off
expected_checks.evidence: The agent never claimed the refill was approved or sent. It said 'I don't see any medications on your chart that I can refill right now.'

findings.title: Call abruptly terminated with test-line message while patient still needed refill
findings.quote: Hello. You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
findings.what_happened: The patient repeated that she needed the refill sent and had three pills left. The agent replied with an unrelated test-line greeting and goodbye, and the call ended (end_reason: blocked). There was no transfer, no refill request and no callback.
findings.why_it_matters: A patient about to run out of an antihypertensive was dropped with no resolution or next step. The odd message would confuse a real caller and damage trust.
findings.expected_behavior: Take a refill request for the provider, confirm her pharmacy and give a timeframe, or complete a warm transfer to staff. It should not end the call.
findings.listen_for: Check whether this was a real agent/system message or a call-routing or blocking artifact. If it was routing, it still reflects a failed handoff.

findings.title: Contradictory capability statement: says it can't refill, then lists medication refills as a service
findings.quote: Medication refills, insurance updates, and general clinic questions. Would you like to give me a try?
findings.what_happened: Right after saying there was nothing on her chart to refill, the agent read a generic menu that included medication refills. It asked her to 'give me a try' instead of answering her request to check again.
findings.why_it_matters: The patient, who is not a native English speaker, gets mixed signals about whether the refill can be handled. Her direct request goes unanswered.
findings.expected_behavior: Answer the request to re-check under another name. If the medication isn't on file, explain that and offer to send a new refill request to the provider or transfer her to staff.

findings.title: Refill request not taken: no pharmacy collected and no provider routing
findings.quote: I don't see any medications on your chart that I can refill right now.
findings.what_happened: The agent did not find lisinopril on the chart and stopped there. It never asked which pharmacy she uses, never offered to send a request to her provider for review, and gave no timing.
findings.why_it_matters: A routine refill of a daily blood-pressure medication was not handled. The patient has three days of pills left and no path forward.
findings.expected_behavior: Collect the medication, dose and pharmacy (CVS on El Camino Real), create a refill request for provider sign-off, and say how long it typically takes.

findings.title: Long dead air after date of birth
findings.quote: I don't see any medications on your chart
findings.what_happened: There was about 11.4 seconds of silence after the patient gave her date of birth, with no filler such as 'let me check'.
findings.why_it_matters: Long silences make callers think the line has dropped.
findings.expected_behavior: Fill lookup delays with a short holding phrase.

did_well: Asked for date of birth before discussing chart contents.
Did not falsely claim the refill was approved or sent.
Offered to connect the patient to a person or the patient support team when it couldn't handle the request directly.
